description: Static website (Astro, i18n with a typed dictionary, content collections) deployed by Cloudflare Pages' Git integration. No tags: PRs land on the default branch `test` (preview), the owner promotes to `main` (production) by fast-forward.

placeholders.AGENT_CHECKS:
`npm ci`, then `npm run build` (runs `astro check`, `astro build`,
the link check and the CSP check). A content or text change in one
language needs the same keys in every dictionary under `src/i18n/`.
placeholders.AGENT_TOOLS: Bash(npm ci*),Bash(npm run build*),Bash(npm run check*),Bash(npx astro check*)

placeholders.HOLD_EXAMPLES: e.g. a visible layout, design or wording change the issue leaves open, a changed URL that other sites link to, the CSP in `public/_headers` or the indexing switches in `src/config.ts`; a visible change the issue specifies exactly is merged, since it reaches the preview only and the owner checks the preview before promoting
placeholders.VERSION_SYNC_RULE:
there is no version number; a deployment is identified by its commit
  (`/build.json`). What must stay in sync instead: a committed generated
  file (an image, a PDF, a data file built from other sources) carries a
  fingerprint of its sources, and a check in `npm run build` fails when
  they drift. Flag a diff that changes such sources without the
  regenerated file and its fingerprint.
placeholders.CHANGELOG_GUARD_RULE:
**No changelog** — this repo has none. Flag a diff that adds a
  `CHANGELOG.md` or a version bump; the PR title is the record.
placeholders.CHANGELOG_RULES:
### No changelog, no versions

A website is not installed, so there is no `CHANGELOG.md`, no version
number and no tag. The record is the history itself:

- **PR titles** on `@@BRANCH@@` (squash-merged, Conventional Commits, e.g.
  `feat(content): add the about page`). Write the title for the owner who
  decides whether to promote: what changes for a visitor.
- **The deployment history** in Cloudflare Pages: every deployment names
  its branch and commit, and `/build.json` on the live site says which
  commit it serves.
placeholders.BUG_LOGS_HINT: The page URL, what you expected, what you saw; browser console output (F12 → Console) if something does not load.
placeholders.STRUCTURE:
src/
├── config.ts             # SITE_URL, PREVIEW (from CF_PAGES_BRANCH), NOINDEX
├── i18n/                 # types.ts (Dictionary, LOCALES), de.ts, en.ts
├── content.config.ts     # zod schemas of the content collections
├── content/posts/        # one Markdown file per post
├── layouts/ components/  # page shell, one component per page
├── lib/                  # helpers (posts, URLs)
└── pages/                # routes: one line per language around a component
public/_headers           # CSP, cache rules, noindex on *.pages.dev
scripts/                  # check-links, check-csp (build), deploy-status (manual)
docs/adr/                 # decisions
placeholders.RELEASE_STEPS:
There are no tags and no GitHub releases. Releasing means promoting
the tested `@@BRANCH@@` to `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@`:

| Branch | Cloudflare Pages serves | Who writes |
|---|---|---|
| `@@BRANCH@@` (default branch) | @@PREVIEW_URL@@ (banner, noindex) | PRs, by humans and agents |
| `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@` | @@SITE_URL@@ | the owner only, by fast-forward |

1. **Land on `@@BRANCH@@`.** Every change is a PR into `@@BRANCH@@` with a
   green `Build and check`. Pages rebuilds the preview within a minute or
   two of the merge.
2. **Show the preview.** Name the changed pages with direct links on
   @@PREVIEW_URL@@; for a visible change add a screenshot.
   `npm run deploy:status -- --preview` confirms the preview serves the
   merged commit.
3. **Wait for approval.** Approval is the owner saying explicitly that this
   state of `@@BRANCH@@` should go live ("promote", "ship it"). A green CI, an
   auto-merge into `@@BRANCH@@`, an approved PR, "looks good" on a wording or a
   direction is **not** approval. Agents never promote.
4. **Promote** (owner, own login), fast-forward only:

   ```
   git switch @@BRANCH@@ && git pull --ff-only
   git push origin @@BRANCH@@:@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@
   ```

   `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@` is protected: no force push, linear history, and the
   commit needs a green `Build and check` (it has one from its run on
   `@@BRANCH@@`). If the push is rejected as non-fast-forward, `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@` has
   commits `@@BRANCH@@` lacks: bring them into `@@BRANCH@@` by PR, check the preview,
   ask again.
5. **Verify live.** `npm run deploy:status` waits until @@SITE_URL@@ serves
   `origin/@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@` and fails otherwise (a failed Pages build silently
   keeps the previous deployment online). Then open the changed pages on
   the live site.

Only part of `@@BRANCH@@` approved? Do not cherry-pick onto `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@`;
revert the rest on `@@BRANCH@@` (a PR) and promote that. To roll back, revert on
`@@BRANCH@@` and promote again; a rollback in the Pages dashboard is for
emergencies and leaves `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@` and the live site apart until the
next promotion.
placeholders.TESTING:
- `npm ci` once (Node version from `.nvmrc`, the same Cloudflare uses).
- **Everything**: `npm run build`, the command CI and Cloudflare Pages run:
  `astro check` (types, i18n parity, content schemas), `astro build`, then
  `scripts/check-links.mjs` (every internal link and `#anchor` in `dist/`
  resolves) and `scripts/check-csp.mjs` (nothing inline the CSP would
  block). A red build is never deployed.
- **Types only**: `npm run check`.
- **As a preview**: `CF_PAGES_BRANCH=@@BRANCH@@ npm run build && npm run preview`
  shows the banner, the noindex tag and the closed `robots.txt`.
- Nothing in the build touches the network. `scripts/deploy-status.mjs`
  does, so it is a manual step of the release and never runs in CI.
placeholders.TYPE_RULES:
### Site rules

- **Never commit or push to `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@`.** Work and PRs go to `@@BRANCH@@`;
  only the owner promotes (Release procedure).
- **Telemetry off**: run Astro with `ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` in the
  environment (CI sets it; set it in your shell and in the Cloudflare Pages
  project), otherwise every build reports to Astro's telemetry endpoint.
- **Every language, every key**: texts live in `src/i18n/<locale>.ts`, typed
  as `Dictionary` (`src/i18n/types.ts`). Add a key to all dictionaries in
  the same change; `astro check` fails otherwise. No text in components.
- **Content follows its schema** (`src/content.config.ts`). A new field
  goes into the schema first, with a comment saying what it is for.
- **Nothing inline**: `<script>` and `<style>` in components are fine
  (Astro bundles them into files), but no `is:inline`, no `style=` or
  `on*=` attributes, no `set:html` with markup from elsewhere. The CSP in
  `public/_headers` would block them in production only;
  `scripts/check-csp.mjs` fails the build first. A new external source
  (font, embed, analytics) is a CSP exception with a comment in
  `public/_headers` and needs the owner.
- **Owner's switches**: `NOINDEX` in `src/config.ts`, the CSP and
  `public/_headers` change only on the owner's explicit request. A preview
  must stay closed to search engines (`PREVIEW`, checked in CI).
- **URLs are public API**: renaming or removing a page breaks links from
  elsewhere; add a redirect in `public/_redirects` in the same PR.
placeholders.CHANGELOG_PR_LINE: I have checked the change on the preview deployment
placeholders.CHANGELOG_TASK_LINE: Checked on the preview deployment (link in the PR)
placeholders.RELEASE_ADR_LINE: - **Promotion instead of tag releases**: work lands on `@@BRANCH@@`, which deploys a preview; a human approves the preview and fast-forwards `@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@` (`git push origin @@BRANCH@@:@@PRODUCTION_BRANCH@@`), then verifies the live site. No tags, no changelog.
placeholders.AGENT_SETUP:
# The agent runs the repo's checks itself.
- uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
  if: steps.token.outputs.present == 'true'
  with:
    node-version-file: .nvmrc

post_render: npm install   # creates package-lock.json, commit it
git init -b test   # test is the default branch; github-setup.py creates main from it

Cloudflare Pages: connect the repo (Git integration); production branch main; build command `npm run build`; output directory `dist`; env ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1; preview branches: test (or all, then PR branches get previews too)
optional: add the Cloudflare Pages check to required_checks in branch protection once it has reported once
if the Pages project name differs from the repo name, render with --set PAGES_PROJECT=<name> (preview URL)
